article_text:
Até 2024, a sagaliterária havia vendido mais de seis milhões de exemplares.

Segundo o THR , a Paramount adquiriu os direitos de “ Fúria Vermelha ” para uma adaptação cinematográfica. O filme terá direção de Francis Lawrence , de “Jogos Vorazes”, e roteiro de Justin Rhodes .

Uma mistura de mitologia romana com ficção científica, “Fúria Vermelha” se passa em Marte, em um futuro no qual a sociedade está organizada em um sistema de classes codificado por cores, com os “Dourados” — a elite superior — no topo. A história gira em torno de Darrow, um jovem mineiro pertencente aos “Vermelhos”, a classe mais baixa, composta por pessoas que existem apenas para realizar trabalhos pesados. Após ver sua amada morrer e descobrir a verdade sobre sua própria existência, Darrow infiltra-se na sociedade dos Dourados com o objetivo de derrubá-la.

Até o momento, seis livros foram publicados, com um sétimo a caminho. Até 2024, a saga “Fúria Vermelha” havia vendido mais de seis milhões de exemplares. Antes da Paramount, a obra chegou a ser cogitada para uma adaptação pela Universal e, no fim da década de 2010, foi cogitada para uma série.

Francis Lawrence tem vasta experiência com franquias de ficção científica distópicas, tendo comandado todos os filmes da saga “Jogos Vorazes” até agora. Ele e o roteirista Justin Rhodes também trabalham juntos na série de “BioShock” para a Netflix.

Ainda não há previsão de estreia para a adaptação de “Fúria Vermelha”.

article_text:
HBO Max renueva su catálogo en octubre con nuevas series, películas, documentales, realities y una programación especial de terror por Halloween.

Octubre llega a HBO Max con una programación cargada de series, películas, documentales, realities y propuestas especiales para Halloween. Entre las principales novedades aparecen producciones originales, historias basadas en hechos reales y varios títulos de terror.

El mes también tendrá un estreno muy especial para la plataforma: Epitafios , la primera producción original de HBO realizada en América Latina, regresa en una versión remasterizada para celebrar los 35 años de HBO en la región.

Series

Guerra – 1 de octubre

Archie Renaux, Dominic West y Sienna Miller protagonizan este drama legal ambientado en el mundo de los grandes abogados de Londres. La historia enfrenta a dos prestigiosos estudios jurídicos mientras un joven abogado queda atrapado en una batalla marcada por la ambición, el poder y la traición.

Estado de Furia – Temporada 2 – 9 de octubre

La segunda temporada presenta nuevas historias protagonizadas por mujeres que quedan atrapadas en un sistema donde las situaciones extremas pueden transformarse en un espectáculo. Maribel Verdú, Carmen Maura, María León y Cecilia Suárez forman parte del elenco.

Epitafios – versión remasterizada – 15 de octubre

Para celebrar sus 35 años en América Latina, HBO recupera su primera producción original realizada en la región. Julio Chávez, Paola Krum, Antonio Birabent y Cecilia Roth protagonizan esta historia policial sobre una serie de asesinatos conectados con una antigua tragedia.

Te puede interesar

Las 5 series y películas para ver este fin de semana en streaming

Qué ver este fin de semana: 4 películas y series que son tendencia en Netflix, HBO Max, Prime Video y Disney+

El colombiano de Keko – 22 de octubre

Juan Cruz, Christian Tappan y Juan Pablo Raba protagonizan este drama basado en hechos reales. Andrés Ballesteros viaja a Tanzania en busca del amor, pero termina encarcelado injustamente por una acusación de narcotráfico y pasa ocho años intentando regresar a su hogar.

Documentales y true crime

Tragedia en el Estadio de La Corregidora – 15 de octubre

Este documental de HBO reconstruye los violentos acontecimientos ocurridos durante un partido entre Querétaro y Atlas en 2022. A través de testimonios inéditos y material nunca antes visto, la producción vuelve sobre las dudas y controversias que quedaron alrededor de aquella jornada.

Poeta Caníbal – octubre

El documental se mete en la historia de José Luis Calva Zepeda, conocido como “El Poeta Caníbal”, y reconstruye el caso a partir de testimonios exclusivos y una investigación sobre los crímenes que conmocionaron a México.

La Masacre de Flores – octubre

La serie documental reconstruye uno de los casos criminales más impactantes de Argentina a través de la historia de Matías Bagnato, único sobreviviente del incendio que terminó con la vida de sus padres, sus dos hermanos y un amigo en 1994.

Películas

Los domingos – 16 de octubre

Ainara tiene 17 años y, mientras su familia espera que decida qué carrera universitaria estudiar, la joven sorprende a todos al revelar que quiere convertirse en monja de clausura. La decisión pone a prueba los vínculos familiares. El elenco incluye a Blanca Soroa, Patricia López Arnaiz y Juan Minujín.

The Moment – 30 de octubre

Charli xcx protagoniza esta película sobre una estrella emergente del pop que debe enfrentarse a las presiones de la fama y de la industria musical mientras prepara su primera gira en grandes estadios. También participan Rosanna Arquette, Kate Berlant, Kylie Jenner y Rachel Sennott.

Realities

MasterChef: Profesionales Brasil – Temporada 6 – 9 de octubre

La versión brasileña del popular reality culinario vuelve con nuevos cocineros profesionales que deberán convencer a tres reconocidos chefs para quedarse con la victoria. El jurado está integrado por Erick Jacquin, Helena Rizzo y Henrique Fogaça.

Supervivencia al Desnudo: Brasil – Temporada 4 – 18 de octubre

Diez participantes intentarán sobrevivir en una región de Sudáfrica atravesada por una histórica sequía y poblada por animales peligrosos, entre ellos búfalos y mambas negras.

Comedia

Kate Berlant: Parmesano – 23 de octubre

La comediante Kate Berlant llega con un especial de HBO Original en el que aborda con humor y sarcasmo temas como la tecnología, la sexualidad y las contradicciones de la vida moderna.

Animación infantil

Hora de Aventura: Misiones Secundarias – 5 de octubre

Finn y Jake regresan a los primeros días de sus aventuras en una nueva serie de episodios autoconclusivos que recupera a varios personajes clásicos de la franquicia, incluido el Rey Helado.

Especial de Halloween

HBO Max también prepara una programación especial para octubre con varias propuestas de terror.

Evil Dead: En llamas – 9 de octubre

Una reunión familiar en una casa aislada se transforma en una pesadilla cuando sus integrantes comienzan a convertirse en Deadites . La película está dirigida por Sébastien Vaniček y cuenta con Souheila Yacoub y Hunter Doohan en su elenco.

Mother Mary – 23 de octubre

Anne Hathaway y Michaela Coel protagonizan esta película dirigida por David Lowery. La historia sigue a una icónica estrella del pop que se reencuentra con su antigua amiga y diseñadora de vestuario antes de regresar a los escenarios.

La herencia de Hope Hill – 23 de octubre

Una joven abogada viaja a Jamaica para investigar una disputa por una herencia, pero descubre que la propiedad involucrada está relacionada con las pesadillas que la persiguen y con un oscuro pasado familiar.

Devorador de almas – 23 de octubre

Un viaje de fin de semana a una mansión aislada en Irlanda se convierte en una pesadilla cuando una antigua criatura de la mitología irlandesa despierta y comienza a infectar a los protagonistas.

Además, durante octubre se suman otros títulos de terror como No te sueltes, Fear Factor: la casa del miedo, Junji Ito: Historias Extrañas para Noches de Insomnio, El Tormento, Noche Infernal, Cacería, Spree: Viaje Desenfrenado, Campeonato de Reposteros: Halloween, A Ciegas, El Carnicero y Los Cazamuertos .

Más estrenos de HBO Max en octubre

Series: La Favorita 1922 T2 (2/10), The Paper T2 (próximamente), Tip Toe (16/10, fecha por confirmar) y Georgie y Mandy – Su Primer Matrimonio T3 (22/10).

Películas: Un Pastel para el Presidente (2/10), Vieja Loca (2/10), Ninotchka (7/10), El Bazar de las Sorpresas (7/10), Maridos (7/10) y ¡Súper Agente Hitpig! (16/10).

Documentales y docuseries: Miller Night Football (3/10), Revista People investiga: sobreviviendo al asesino T2 (6/10), Mi relación con un asesino serial (7/10), Cuando Nadie me ve (9/10), Tierra de Crimen (12/10), Epic: Elvis Presley in Concert (16/10), Narco Hack (23/10), Sister Wives T14 (26/10) y Kordell: Slash & Burn (31/10), entre otros.

Animación: El Maravillosamente Extraño Mundo de Gumball T2 (9/10), Solo Necesitas Matar (9/10), Tom and Jerry Gokko Compilation-2 (23/10), Regular Show Presents: Terror Tales of the Park VII Halloween (4/10), Get Jiro (3/10), Gachiakuta (12/10) y Dragon Ball Beerus (16/10).

editorial_title_zh: 英国反法西斯艺术的故事
editorial_excerpt_zh: 今天的我们，是否还拥有这些艺术家当年奋起抗争时哪怕一半的能量？

"这场全面而令人痛切地切中当下的英国政治艺术调查，聚焦于第二次世界大战前夕及战时创作的作品，开篇是1933年激进左翼、反法西斯、且广泛持和平主义立场的艺术家国际协会（AIA）的成立。这是40年来首次对这一群体进行梳理，通过艺术作品、文献资料和当时的 ephemera（印刷品），轻快地突出了11位关键人物的创作。有一张醒目的黑白照片，照片中是留着时髦波波头的作家兼艺术家Pearl Binder，还有一张画家Margaret和James Fitton的合影——这对目光坚毅的夫妇燃烧着意识形态的激情。你也许会不无惆怅地想起沃伦·比蒂1981年的电影《赤色分子》，以及片中那群西方老一代人、坚定的实证主义左派、老布尔什维克：那些在斯大林大清洗和1932–33年毁灭性的乌克兰大饥荒为公众所知之前，以西方人的眼光看待俄罗斯的人。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在历史时间线上对这些灾难有所认识之前，我们看到Cliff Rowe的《失业者与警察部队之间的斗争》（1933），这是一幅如今藏于利沃夫的巨幅、如梦似幻的画作的半尺寸复制品。这幅画构思于莫斯科，场景却设在伦敦，描绘了愤怒的饥饿游行者与大都会警察之间的激战。Rowe本人也客串出场，在喧闹的特拉法加广场上与警察扭打，双层巴士顶上还有旁观者俯瞰；后来，在《炸鱼店》（1936）中，他古怪地想象斯大林在北伦敦大口吃薯条。作为反偶像者中的反偶像者，Rowe嘲讽了1935年的银禧庆典，制作了一张海报，把乔治五世画成戴王冠的骷髅，下颌滴着血，配文是：25年的战争 饥饿 失业。（你还以为性手枪乐队够大胆？）Pearl Binder也去过莫斯科：她那组极具感染力的石版画同样出自1935年，画中她与苏联水兵嬉闹，随后回到家中与那些“在工作室派对上闲站”的布卢姆斯伯里圈中人厮混。有些事永远不会变。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://backend.artreview.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Henrion-For-Liberty-1230x1887.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "FHK Henrion，《为了自由》，1943，海报设计。承蒙Henrion遗产、FHK Henrion档案馆及布莱顿大学档案馆惠允", "credit": "ArtReview", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "到1936年，随着佛朗哥在西班牙崛起，抗击法西斯主义的紧迫性加剧。Felicia Browne是志愿者之一，还没等到丧钟为她敲响；她在萨拉戈萨附近中弹身亡。她失而复得的速写本中的页面，展示了对战友们简洁有力的线条描绘，预示着共和国的胜利与悲剧。如果说这里会让人想到乔治·奥威尔的回忆录《向加泰罗尼亚致敬》（1938），那么这位作家在别处还有更多回响：James Boswell 1933年那组大胆而噩梦般的画作《伦敦的陷落》，预示了《上来透口气》（1939）中George Bowling对空中轰炸的可怕预感。我们看到一个人吊在绞刑架上，脱轨的列车，人群冲击圣保罗大教堂周围的街垒；而Boswell其他讽刺权贵的漫画，则使他成为乔治·格罗斯更为文雅的英国兄弟。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "并非全是阴郁和悲观。这里还有Margaret article_text:
Do we, today, possess even half the energy these artists had to fight?

This comprehensive and painfully relevant survey of British political art made just before and during the Second World War begins with the establishment of the radical leftist, antifascist, widely pacifist Artists International Association (AIA) in 1933. In the first survey of this grouping in 40 years, the work of 11 key players is briskly highlighted through art, documentation and period ephemera. There’s a striking monochrome photograph of stylishly bobbed writer/artist Pearl Binder, along with a shot of painters Margaret and James Fitton, a steely-eyed couple burning with ideological intensity. You might be reminded, not without melancholy, of Warren Beatty’s 1981 film Reds and its chorus of Occidental ancients, determinedly positivistic leftists, old Bolshevists: those who saw Russia through Western eyes before public knowledge of Stalin’s purges and the devastating Ukrainian famine of 1932–33.

Preceding the recognition of these disasters in the historical timeline, we see Cliff Rowe’s The Struggle Between the Unemployed and the Police Forces (1933), a half-size reproduction of a huge, hallucinatory canvas now held in Lviv. Conceived in Moscow but set in London, this depicts a pitched battle between angry marchers against hunger and the Metropolitan Police. Rowe plays a cameo, up for a ruck with the fuzz in a noisy Trafalgar Square overseen by onlookers atop a double-decker bus; later, in The Fried Fish Shop (1936), he weirdly imagines Stalin scarfing chips in North London. An iconoclast’s iconoclast, Rowe mocked the Silver Jubilee of 1935 by making a poster of George V seen as a crowned skull, jaw dripping blood, with the legend: 25 YEARS OF WAR HUNGER UNEMPLOYMENT. (And you thought the Sex Pistols were daring?) Pearl Binder also visited Moscow: her brilliantly evocative set of lithographs, also from 1935, see her cavorting with Soviet sailors before heading home to hang out with Bloomsbury types who ‘stood around at studio parties’. Some things never change.

By 1936, the imperative to fight fascism was heightened by Franco’s rise in Spain. Felicia Browne was one of the volunteers before the bells tolled for her; she was gunned down near Zaragoza. Pages from her recovered sketchbook show pithily lined drawings of fellow combatants anticipating the triumphs and tragedies of the Republic. If one might think, here, of George Orwell’s memoir Homage to Catalonia (1938), there are more echoes of the author elsewhere, with the ghastly aerial-bombardment premonitions of George Bowling in Coming Up for Air (1939) prefigured in James Boswell’s 1933 sequence of daring, nightmarish drawings, The Fall of London . We see a man hanging from a gibbet, derailed trains, crowds storming barricades around St. Paul’s; while Boswell’s other caricatures of posh toffs mark him as a politer English sibling to George Grosz.

It’s not all doom and gloom. There are some delicate oils by Margaret Fitton: softly textured domestic scenes from a then bosky Dulwich, peacefully nostalgic kitchen cookery as with the mid-1930s Rhubarb Pie ; you can almost smell a cloying reek. Elsewhere a government poster on rationing urges: ‘A clear plate means a clear conscience’. But the overwhelmingly serious message from this darkly sobering time-capsule of a show is that the twentieth-century battle against fascism demanded an iron will and indomitable persistence, slog and sacrifice. As resurgent fascism threatens, we might ask if we possess even half the energy these artists had to fight, the means and the will, that helped them win after 12 long years.

Comrades in Art: Artists Against Fascism at Towner, Eastbourne, 7 May – 18 October

article_text:
Walter Koenig ‘s “Star Trek” colleagues are remembering the actor who played Chekov in the original “Star Trek” series, calling him “a loyal friend.” Koenig died Sunday in Los Angeles. His “Star Trek” co-star George Takei reminisced over Koenig serving as best man at his wedding.

Takei, who played Lieutenant Hikaru Sulu, wrote on Instagram, “My heart is heavy. Walter Koenig, our Ensign Pavel Chekov, passed away early today.

Brian Gordon Takes Executive Producer, Head of Live Content Roles at PGA Tour Studios

“Walter and I met on the bridge of the Enterprise in the 1960s, and we stayed friends for nearly six decades,” the post continued. “When Brad and I married in 2008, Walter stood beside us as our best man. Just last month, on Sept. 14, he turned 90, on the same day Brad and I celebrated our 18th wedding anniversary. I will always treasure that he and I shared that date. Walter was more than Chekov. He was a writer, a teacher, a thoughtful man, and a loyal friend. To the fans who loved him for so many years, thank you. He loved you too. Rest well, my dear friend. Keep navigating a steady course.”

View this post on Instagram

Adam Nimoy, Leonard Nimoy’s son, wrote, “So sad to hear about the loss of Walter Koenig. Such a nice guy and when we were on the convention circuit together a pleasure to hang out with. Here he is with Celeste Yarnall in ‘The Apple,’ one of my favorites of the oddball episodes. Farewell.”

So sad to hear about the loss of Walter Koenig. Such a nice guy and when we were on the convention circuit together a pleasure to hang out with. Here he is with Celeste Yarnall in “The Apple”, one of my favorites of the oddball episodes. Farewell. pic.twitter.com/NuUJvHgR3h — Adam Nimoy (@adam_nimoy) October 26, 2026

Michael Okuda, a scenic artist and technical consultant on several “Star Trek” installments, recalled his interview for the Roddenberry archive, writing , “Mourning the passing of Star Trek legend Walter Koenig. He was 90. A couple of years ago, Walter gave us a nice interview for the Roddenberry Archive.”

Koenig’s reps said in a statement, “Today we mourn the passing of Walter Koenig, whose talent, warmth, and unforgettable performances left a lasting mark on generations of fans around the world. He passed of old age at home in North Hollywood last night surrounded by his daughter and niece.

“Best known for his iconic role as Pavel Chekov in ‘Star Trek: The Original Series,’ Walter helped inspire audiences with his optimism, humor, and adventurous spirit. Beyond ‘Star Trek,’ his long and distinguished career showcased his versatility as an actor and his genuine love for his craft. His remarkable talent continued to shine in his later years, most recently with his performance in the short film ‘Mr. Fleischmann,’ for which he received the Platinum Award for Best Actor at the 2026 Independent Shorts Awards — a fitting recognition of a lifetime devoted to his craft…

“Thank you, Walter, for the memories, the inspiration, and for boldly going where few have gone before.”

editorial_excerpt_zh: 又到这个季节了！《恋爱假期》将于12月11日重返影院，以庆祝这部浪漫喜剧上映20周年。该片由卡梅隆·迪亚茨、裘德·洛、凯特·温丝莱特和杰克·布莱克主演，这部2006年经典节日电影的官方剧情简介写道：“艾瑞丝（温丝莱特饰）爱上了一个即将迎娶其他女人的男人。在地球的另一端，阿曼达（迪亚茨饰）发现与她同居的男人一直不忠。两个素未谋面、相距6,000英里远的女人，发现自己处在完全相同的境地。她们在一个房屋交换网站上相识，并在一时冲动之下在假期互换了住所。艾瑞丝搬进了阿曼达位于阳光加州洛杉矶的房子，而阿曼达则来到了白雪皑皑的英国乡间。在抵达目的地后不久，两个女人都遇到了她们既不想要也未曾料到的东西：一段新的恋情。阿曼达被艾瑞丝英俊的哥哥格雷厄姆（洛饰）所吸引，而艾瑞丝在传奇编剧阿瑟（伊莱·瓦拉赫饰）的启发下，在遇到电影配乐师迈尔斯（布莱克饰）时治愈了心碎。”

article_text:
‘Tis the season! “ The Holiday ” is returning to theaters on Dec. 11 to celebrate the romantic comedy’s 20th anniversary.

Starring Cameron Diaz, Jude Law, Kate Winslet and Jack Black, the official logline for the 2006 holiday classic reads: “Iris (Winslet) is in love with a man who is about to marry another woman. Across the globe, Amanda (Diaz), realizes the man she lives with has been unfaithful. Two women who have never met and live 6,000 miles apart, find themselves in the exact same place. They meet online at a home exchange website and impulsively switch homes for the holiday. Iris moves into Amanda’s LA house in sunny California as Amanda arrives in the snow covered English countryside. Shortly after arriving at their destinations, both women find the last thing either wants or expects: a new romance. Amanda is charmed by Iris’ handsome brother Graham (Law) and Iris, with inspiration provided by legendary screenwriter Arthur (Eli Wallach), mends her heart when she meets film composer Miles (Black).”

Related Stories

'I Play Rocky' Star Anthony Ippolito on Becoming Sylvester Stallone and Acting With a Dog: 'He Wasn't a Huge Fan of Me'

‘Wildwood’ Director Travis Knight on AI: 'An Amazing Piece of Technology’ but ‘I’m Not Embracing It at All’

Along with its return to theaters, a limited series adaptation of the movie is in development at Apple TV. The series would focus on different characters, but center on two women, one British and one American, who swap houses during the Christmas season and find love along the way.

Upon its initial release, “The Holiday” was a box office success, grossing over $200 million worldwide. It has maintained a strong, festive fandom ever since. “The Holiday” is written and directed by Nancy Meyers. It is produced by Columbia Pictures and Universal Pictures in association with Relativity Media and Waverly Films Production.

article_text:
The Cat in the Hat was no match for the mighty Godzilla. “ Godzilla Minus Zero ” climbed to the top of box office charts with $31.6 million from 3,254 theaters, a roaring start for a foreign language epic in North America. Meanwhile “The Cat in the Hat” stumbled with $20 million from 4,003 locations, a weak debut for an animated movie that’s based on one of the most well-known children’s books of all time.

Ticket sales for “Godzilla Minus Zero” register as the largest opening for a live-action foreign language film in North America. The R-rated monster movie benefitted from sterling reviews and strong audience scores (a 90% on Rotten Tomatoes and “A” grade on CinemaScore exit polls), as well as outsized interest from premium large formats. It’s the first Japanese production ever filmed for Imax, and the company’s bigger and brighter screens have contributed a huge $12.7 million, or, 40% of domestic grosses. It wasn’t just Imax that appealed to audiences. PLFs, including Dolby, accounted for a staggering 74% of ticket sales. By comparison, “The Odyssey” collected 53% of opening weekend returns from PLFs.

Related Stories

'I Swear' Star Robert Aramayo on the BAFTA N-Word Incident That Overshadowed the Movie and the ‘X-Men’ Wolverine Pitch He Keeps Hearing

Lucy Liu’s 'The Pirate Queen' Expands With Graphic Novel, New Game and International Tour as Creator Eloise Singer Joins BAFTA Breakthrough Cohort (EXCLUSIVE)

“We’re so happy to see audiences embrace ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ at an unprecedented scale for an international film,” says Chance Huskey, VP of distribution for Gkids, which distributed the movie in the U.S. “This landmark release is the result of a thoughtful campaign by Gkids and Toho that emphasized the ‘must see’ intensity of the theatrical experience.”

“Godzilla Minus Zero” built on the success of the prior kaiju adventure, 2023’s “Godzilla Minus One.” That sci-fi epic secured a better-than-expected $11.4 million start and powered to $57 million in North America and $113 million globally, in addition to winning a visual effects Oscar. Produced by Japan’s Toho and directed by Takashi Yamazaki, the movie takes place two years after the previous installment as Godzilla regenerates and resurfaces to combat a new monster that’s tormenting postwar Japan.

“‘Godzilla’ is a hit,” says David A. Gross, who publishes the box office newsletter FranchiseRe. “Critics’ reviews and audience scores are once again outstanding. This weekend’s opening takes the Japanese production to a new level.”

“The Cat in the Hat” was well-received by audiences, earning an “A” grade on CinemaScore, which could help in terms of box office longevity. Critics weren’t as kind, saddling the movie with a 45% on Rotten Tomatoes. Bill Hader voices the titular character in the cartooned version, which revolves around the shenanigans that occur after a mischievous cat (wearing a hat) arrives to cheer up two siblings who move to a new town. Overseas, “The Cat in the Hat” collected just $10 million from 60 international markets for a global start of $30.5 million. Unless “The Cat in the Hat” rebounds in the coming weeks, the $92 million-budgeted movie will rank as another dud for Warner Bros. (Theater owners keep roughly 50% of ticket sales.) The studio, which recently merged with Paramount Skydance, has endured a brutal year at the box office with flops, including “Digger,” “The Bride!” and “Supergirl,” which have resulted in hundreds of millions in theatrical losses.

“This is a soft opening,” Gross says. “However, family animation does extremely well in ancillary windows, earning more in digital sales and rental, streaming and TV licensing than in theatrical. That is where the film should recover its costs.”

This is the second adaptation of the Dr. Seuss classic following 2003’s live-action comedy, starring Mike Myers as the Cat. That film opened to $38 million, not adjusted for inflation, and ran out of steam with $134 million, a disappointing result given the budget was above $100 million. More recently, Dr. Seuss adaptations like 2018’s “The Grinch” (which opened to $67 million) and 2012’s “The Lorax” (which opened to $70 million) were big hits for Universal and Illumination. Yes, the theatrical landscape has changed a lot since those films were released. But “The Cat in the Hat” is based on popular IP, and it didn’t have any competition. (Families with young kids haven’t had much to see since since Universal’s “Forgotten Island” in September.) Even this spring’s “Hoppers,” an original offering from Disney and Pixar, managed to debut to $45 million.

Overall, this weekend reached $114 million across all films, up 86% from the same frame a year ago when “Predator: Badlands” was No. 1 at the box office. Meanwhile, year-to-date revenues hit $8.6 billion, 20% above the same point in 2025, according to Rentrak. Exhibitors are hoping the momentum continues through November, which sees the release of Paramount’s Christmas fantasy “Ebenezer,” starring Johnny Depp, Lionsgate’s “Hunger Games” prequel “Sunrise on the Reaping,” Universal’s comedy “Focker in Law,” with Ariana Grande joining Ben Stiller and Robert De Niro, and Disney’s animated “Hexed.”

“It’s another encouraging sign as we head toward the all-important holiday movie season,” says Rentrak’s head of marketplace trends Paul Dergarabedian.

Also this weekend, Searchlight’s dark comedy “Wild Horse Nine,” starring John Malkovich and Sam Rockwell and directed by Martin McDonagh, opened at No. 8 with $6 million from 1,100 theaters. It’s a promising debut for the Oscar hopeful, which has a much larger initial footprint than McDonagh’s prior film, 2022’s “The Banshees of Inisherin.” After starting in limited release, “Banshees of Inisherin” became a slow and steady box office hit with $10.5 million domestically and $50 million globally. “Wild Horse Nine” follows Malkovich and Rockwell as CIA officers who are dispatched from Santiago to Easter Island shortly before a Chilean military coup.

Another newcomer, the Indian epic “Ramayana: Rise of a Legend,” earned $8.6 million over the traditional weekend and $12.1 million during its first four days in theaters. Sony is distributing “Ramayana: Rise of a Legend” in 1,300 theaters, marking the widest North American release for an Indian film. Nitesh Tiwari‘s two-part adaptation of the ancient Hindu epic are the most expensive Indian films ever made, costing a combined $500 million to bring to screens . Globally, the movie bowed to $55.7 million, led by India with $32 million followed by the United Kingdom with $3 million.

“Indian epics do some business in English-speaking countries, but they can make a fortune in India,” says Gross. “It’s going to need to make a fortune there.”

“Ramayana: Rise of a Legend” opened in fifth place behind of A24’s electric Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything.” The zeitgeist-capturing movie has earned $8.8 million from 2,473 theaters in its fourth weekend of release, boosting its domestic tally to a staggering $79.8 million. “You Can See Everything” will leave theaters as one of the biggest documentaries in decades. And it will be very profitable for A24, which produced the nearly three-hour movie for $7 million.

“Drummer Boy,” a Christian musical from Angel Studios, landed at No. 3 with $9.3 million from 2,850 theaters. “Jimmy,” a faith-based biopic starring KJ Apa as the actor and military vet Jimmy Stewart, finished the weekend in 12th place with just $2.2 million from 1,470 theaters.

Elsewhere, A24’s heartwarming comedy “Club Kid” and Amazon MGM’s drama “I Play Rocky” scored in limited release. “Club Kid” earned $390,583 from six screens in New York and Los Angeles, translating to $65,097 per location. Jordan Firstman wrote, directed and stars in the film, which revolves around a hard-partying club promoter who finds out he has a 10-year-old son. “I Play Rocky” captured $345,000 from seven theaters, averaging $49,200 per location. Directed by Peter Farrelly, the movie depicts the real life story of Sylvester Stallone bringing the 1976 classic “Rocky” to the big screen. Both films will expand nationwide around Thanksgiving.

“We’re incredibly encouraged by the response to ‘I Play Rocky,” so far,” says Amazon MGM Studios head of domestic distribution Kevin Wilson. “The enthusiasm from audiences reinforces our belief that we have a film with both awards potential and commercial appeal.”

More to come…
excerpt_original: The Cat in the Hat was no match for the mighty Godzilla. “Godzilla Minus Zero” climbed to the top of box office charts with $31.6 million from 3,254 theaters, a roaring start for a foreign-language epic in North America. Meanwhile, “The Cat in the Hat” stumbled with $20 million…

"translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": article_text:
Cine

La caída de la ballena – Crítica de la película

Gerardo Frías

Una película visualmente espectacular con mucho corazón.

Quedar atrapado dentro de un cachalote suena a premisa de chiste. Sin embargo, Brian Duffield (director de la película La caída de la ballena ) a partir de la novela de Daniel Kraus, la toma completamente en serio: Jay Gardiner (Austin Abrams) se sumerge frente a la costa de California en busca de los restos de su padre (Josh Brolin) y termina tragado por un cachalote, con apenas una hora de oxígeno para salir con vida.

Lo primero que hay que decir sobre la película La caída de la ballena , es que visualmente le pusieron muchísimo esmero. La secuencia de las orcas atacando al cachalote es un espectáculo maravilloso, de esas escenas que justifican por sí solas la experiencia de verla en pantalla grande. Pero el verdadero peso de la película lo carga Austin Abrams, que sigue demostrando por qué cada vez lo vemos más en los estelares de las ultimas películas mejor valoradas de la cartelera. Su Jay no es el héroe de acción que, con sus magníficas habilidades, escapa del estómago de la ballena; al contrario, lo vemos sufrir de verdad, y sufrimos con él esa desesperación que la atmósfera de la cinta logra crear. A pesar de los flashbacks y las escenas extra, la mayor parte de la película la pasamos junto a él en la estrechez de un espacio mínimo, y Abrams tiene una capacidad enorme de hacernos empatizar con ese encierro.

Y hay algo más que vale la pena destacar tanto de él como de la dirección de la película La caída de la ballena : la manera en que manejan el estrés, la ansiedad y la presión de una escena tensa y, solo con actuación y diálogo, logran sacarle al público risas, tanto nerviosas como de comedia pura. Es algo en lo que Abrams con su autenticidad se está volviendo experto, y aquí lo explotaron muy bien.

Donde la película se queda un poco corta es en la historia. Todo gira en torno a la relación entre Jay y su padre, pero se pasa por encima de ella con tanta rapidez que, en lo personal, nunca llegué a sentirla lo suficientemente explorada como para empatizar de verdad. Y el punto más débil, creo, es el abuso de los flashbacks del padre para que Jay recuerde justo lo que necesita en cada momento. Entiendo que son necesarios para no cansarnos de tener a la ballena como único escenario, y para hacer avanzar la aventura, pero pudieron haberse explorado de otra manera, o incluso dejarnos conocer más del pasado del personaje de Brolin como buzo en su juventud o antes de Jay. Eso habría vuelto la película mucho más emocional, sin tener que caer tan de golpe en que Jay imagine la voz de su padre dentro de la ballena o en recuerdos tan exactos y constantes.

Aun así, es una película para estresarte junto a su protagonista, reír y, quizás, pensar bastante en cuánto juzgamos a nuestros padres. Nadie es perfecto, nadie nace sabiendo cómo ser padre, y al final nos convertimos en quienes somos gracias a ellos, con sus errores y malos momentos, pero con un amor incondicional. Algo que la cinta refleja incluso a través de la fugaz vida de la ballena a lo largo del largometraje. Sin duda disfrutar de la película La caída de la ballena en pantalla grande vale por completo la pena.

Gerardo Frías

article_text:
Announcement

Applications Open for the MFA in Studio Art at Maine College of Art & Design

Apply by January 17, 2027 to be considered for a full-tuition scholarship.

The Master of Fine Arts in Studio Art (MFA) program at Maine College of Art & Design (MECA&D) in Portland, Maine, offers an interdisciplinary approach that encourages students to think across traditional academic boundaries, expand their art practice, and challenge their intellectual curiosity.

Our six-term curriculum emphasizes the intersection of studio practice, individual research, and critical analysis. Built on a commitment to one-on-one student mentoring by distinguished faculty, visiting artists, critics, and curators, MECA&D’s MFA program offers a dynamic and supportive learning environment for artists who want to define and pursue a sustainable and transformative vision for their art practice.

Full and Low Residency

Embedded within our MFA is a level of flexibility, allowing students to choose between Full and Low Residency. MECA&D’s Full Residency option provides 24/7 access to private studios and fabrication facilities where students work alongside peers and faculty. Among the first programs of its kind in the country, MECA&D’s Low Residency option combines intensive periods of on-campus instruction with the freedom and independence of working from home, anywhere in the world. Intensive group sessions, woven throughout our two-year curriculum, bring all MFA students together for research, travel, and dialogue.

Summer intensive in Portland, Maine

All MFA students are in residence in Portland, Maine, for eight weeks each summer. As the first and fourth terms in a six-trimester course of study, these Summer Intensives function as catalysts for community and exchange. Renowned faculty, visiting artists, and critics deliver public lectures, conduct studio visits, and participate in group activities and discussions with graduate candidates during their respective visits to the MECA&D MFA Program.

Application Deadlines

Full-Tuition Scholarship: January 17, 2027

Priority Acceptance: February 21, 2027

Program Start: June 2027

title_original: Sundance 2026: Last Dance
editorial_excerpt_zh: 最终召唤：在这个电影节位于帕克城的最后一届上，许多最佳影片印证了其已故创始人罗伯特·雷德福对“出人意料的视角”的信念。
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "我讨厌闭幕，所以选择远程参加犹他州帕克城的最后一届圣丹斯电影节对我来说不费吹灰之力。反正自COVID-19大流行以来，我一直都是虚拟参加电影节；尽管我非常怀念与那些制作、发行和撰写电影的朋友们实地相聚的某些方面，但我知道，从1989年到2020年每年陪伴我经历的那个圣丹斯，既不会轰轰烈烈地收场，也不会在啜泣中结束。事实上，目前垄断轰鸣与啜泣的，是那些从明尼阿波利斯、基辅、加沙和苏丹发回日常新闻的记者。没有什么能与之相比——对我而言，在家里，也确实没有什么能比。我知道圣丹斯将在科罗拉多州博尔德卷土重来；不知疲倦的米歇尔·萨特会确保与电影节同样至关重要的圣丹斯实验室继续发掘和支持有才华的导演、编剧和制片人；而戴维·林德在独立电影领域拥有漫长而光荣的历史，是运营整个活动的极佳人选。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "但我猜，没有了于2025年逝世的创始之父罗伯特·雷德福，圣丹斯将沦为又一个普通的电影节，一个用来颁发奖项并收获评论的地方——这些奖项和评论对新闻稿很有用，或许能让发行商和/或流媒体向某个无名之辈抛出救命稻草。圣丹斯与众不同之处在于，它是由一位电影明星创立的——他是最后也是最伟大的明星之一——他有些矛盾地坚信，一部电影的价值不由票房收入决定，而是由它所构建的社群决定的。当你的电影在圣丹斯上映时，或者当你在电影节上观看电影时，你就是那个社群的一部分，哪怕你内心的一部分在反抗它。毕竟，“普通的鲍勃”本身也有点反叛精神。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我对圣丹斯最深刻的记忆大多是那些让我心潮澎湃的放映：理查德·凯利的《死亡幻觉》（2001年）、托德·海因斯的《安然无恙》和拉里·克拉克的《半熟少年》（1995年），以及简·坎皮恩七小时的有线电视剧集《谜湖之巅》（2013年），当时只放了几个短场休息，以至于几乎没人有机会去上厕所，因为埃及剧院只有两个洗手间。不过，最让我记忆犹新的是在90年代中期，我在一次与罗伯特·雷德福同台的小组讨论后与他争论。当我像一个痴迷阿尔都塞的研究生一样说我们“被固定在意识形态中”时，他感到很不安。他无法接受我们在这种事情上没有意识的选择。我试图解释，让我困扰的是圣丹斯将“故事”奉为绝对真理的方式。他不同意，但他从未将我的立场记在心里。在为今年许多场次放映开场的前贴片中，雷德福在一处画外音中说道：“我希望，如果我们能为人们提供表达出人意料之视角的契机，那将会开阔人们的眼界与思想。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "据各方报道，在2026年圣丹斯电影节的多部优秀影片中——这一届电影节多次印证了雷德福关于“出人意料的视角”的理念——最受瞩目的当属《哈莱姆往事》，大约一年前我在一场制作中（work-in-progress）放映会上看过它，但遗憾的是，作为远程参会者，我无法看到它的最终完成版。1972年，威廉·格里夫斯——一位以狂野而精明的反身性纪录片《意孪金科：第一辑》（1968年）而闻名的先锋纪录片制片兼导演——邀请了当时依然充满活力的哈莱姆文艺复兴时期的艺术家和思想家参加了一场派对，他们在会上追忆往事、争论不休，将一段充满传奇色彩的过去唤醒为激动人心的现在。格里夫斯于2014年逝世，他始终未能为自己收集的动态影像历史找到一种形式，但曾参与1972年拍摄的他的儿子大卫，决心将长达数小时的16毫米胶片素材剪辑成一部剧情长片。根据我所看到的片段，其成果堪称惊艳。", "到目前为止，我远程观看的最令人印象深刻的电影是世界电影剧情片竞赛单元的获奖作品——由出生于科索沃、常驻德国的导演维萨尔·莫里纳执导的《羞耻与金钱》。出色的演员阿斯特里特·卡巴什和弗洛尼娅·科德利饰演了沙班和他的妻子哈蒂谢，他们经营着一家小型奶牛场，但由于沙班叛逆的弟弟偷走了他们的奶牛，他们被迫搬到了城市。这对夫妇只希望努力工作，抚养他们的孩子和沙班的母亲，但坦白说，无情的资本主义和虚伪的阶级制度却不断破坏沙班的根基，将他逼向崩溃的边缘。莫里纳的风格直截了当，长镜头依赖于演员的表现力以及局势随时可能爆发暴力的潜力。说这让我经常想起早期的法斯宾德和克里斯蒂·普尤，绝不会贬低莫里纳作品的独特性。", article_text:
I hate closings, so it was a no-brainer for me to take the remote option for the last Sundance in Park City, Utah. I have been attending the festival virtually since the COVID-19 pandemic anyway, and although there are aspects of being on the ground with friends who make, distribute, and write about movies that I greatly miss, I knew that Sundance as I had experienced it every year from 1989 to 2020 would go out with neither a bang nor a whimper. Indeed, a near-monopoly on banging and whimpering is at this moment held by those reporting the daily news from Minneapolis, Kyiv, Gaza, and Sudan. Nothing can compare—and for me, at home, nothing did. I know that Sundance will stage a comeback in Boulder, Colorado; that the indefatigable Michelle Satter will make sure the Sundance labs, which are as essential as the festival, will continue to discover and support talented directors, writers, and producers; and that David Linde, with his long, honorable history in independent film, is a very good choice to run the entire shebang.

But I suspect that without its founding father Robert Redford, who died in 2025, Sundance will become just another film festival, a place where movies are anointed with prizes and reviews that are useful in press releases and might make a distributor and/or streamer throw an unknown a lifeline. What has distinguished Sundance is that it was created by a film star—one of the last and greatest of them—who believed, somewhat paradoxically, that the value of a movie was not determined by box-office receipts but by the community it built. When your movie was shown at Sundance, or when you watched movies at the festival, you were part of that community, even if part of you rebelled against it. After all, “Ordinary Bob” was something of a rebel himself.

Most of the indelible memories I have of Sundance are of screenings that thrilled me: Richard Kelly’s Donnie Darko in 2001, Todd Haynes’s Safe and Larry Clark’s Kids in 1995, and Jane Campion’s seven-hour hour cable series Top of the Lake in 2013, shown with only a couple of short breaks so almost no one had a chance to pee because the Egyptian Theater had just two bathrooms. Most of all, however, I remember arguing with Redford sometime in the mid-’90s after I had been on a panel with him. He had been disturbed when I had said, like a grad student enamored of Althusser, that we are “fixed in ideology.” He could not accept that we had no conscious choice in the matter. I tried to explain that I was bothered by the way that Sundance believed in “story” as an absolute. He disagreed, but he never held my position against me. At one point in the trailer that opened many of this year’s screenings, Redford, in voiceover, says, “It is my hope that if we can give people the opportunity to express the unexpected perspective, then that will open eyes and minds.”

By all accounts, among the best films at Sundance 2026, an edition that affirmed Redford’s idea of “the unexpected perspective” several times over, was Once Upon a Time in Harlem , which I saw about a year ago at a work-in-progress screening, but sadly wasn’t available to me as a remote attendee in its finished form. In 1972, William Greaves, a pioneering documentary producer and director best known for his wildly and cannily reflexive Symbiopsychotaxiplasm: Take One (1968), invited still-vital artists and thinkers of the Harlem Renaissance to a party, where they reminisced, argued, and revived a storied past into an exciting present. Greaves, who died in 2014, never found a form for the moving-image history he had collected, but his son, David, who had been part of the 1972 shoot, was determined to turn many hours of 16mm footage into a feature. The result, based on what I’ve seen of it, is brilliant.

By far the most impressive film I saw remotely was the winner of the World Cinema Dramatic Competition: Shame and Money by the Kosovo-born, Germany-based director Visar Morina. The superb actors Astrit Kabashi and Flonja Kodheli play Shaban and his wife Hatixhe, who run a small dairy farm, but are forced to move to the city when their cows are stolen by Shaban’s renegade brother. The couple want only to work hard and provide for their kids and Shaban’s mother, but Shaban is undermined and pushed to the breaking point, to put it bluntly, by ruthless capitalism and the hypocritical class system. Morina’s style is straightforward, with long takes that rely on the expressivity of his actors and the potential of the situation to explode in violence. It should take nothing away from the specificity of Morina’s work to say that I was often reminded of early Fassbinder and Cristi Puiu.

A more stylized critique of power, Rafael Manuel’s first feature, Filipiñana , won a special jury award for creative vision and has been acquired by Jia Zhangke’s new film-distribution company. Set on a vast country-club golf course, a legacy of the American occupation of the Philippines, it is a devastating coming-of-age story focused on a teenager, whose job as a “tee girl” exposes her to exceptionally cruel and perverse exploitation.

As usual, documentaries were a safer bet than the fiction films. Two pleasurable examples, Rachael J. Morrison’s Joybubbles and David Shadrack Smith’s Public Access , deserve a post-Sundance life. Morrison’s portrait of the late Joe Engressia, aka Joybubbles, is a bittersweet construction of home movies, still photos, newspaper clippings, interviews, and, crucially, recordings of Engressia’s voice, which bears a striking similarity to that of David Lynch. Engressia, who was born blind, learned almost by chance how to connect to the world by telephone. Possessing perfect pitch, he could whistle tones in the exact frequencies that rotary phones employed in their dialing system. An instigator of the “phone phreak” subculture, Engressia was first prosecuted by the feds for wire fraud but later became a valued phone-company employee, and, in his last years, began a phone call-in service through which he connected with people who needed to hear a friendly voice on the line. Morrison is too smart to label Joybubbles as the forerunner to the titans of social media, although she includes a priceless clip of the young Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak (themselves inspired by Engressia) toying with the famously illegal “blue box,” which hijacked long-distance phone networks by mimicking their signal tones. Joybubbles has the making of a minor cult classic.

Another exploration of what now seems like primitive tech, Public Access focuses on Channel C, which was born out of the requirement that Manhattan Cable Television, a subsidiary of Time Inc., give something to New York City in exchange for commercial cable rights to much of the metropolis. Channel C was a showcase for the downtown music and art scene of the late ’70s and early ’80s, from Pat Ivers and Emily Armstrong’s Nightclubbing videos and Glenn O’Brien’s TV Party to more salacious spectacles promoted by Screw Magazine’s Al Goldstein in the name of freedom of speech and information. Perhaps Channel C’s most valuable effort was hosting Paper Tiger TV , a no-budget news series crafted by video- and filmmakers who put politics above artistic niceties. Public Access covers a lot of ground without very much depth, but it is a pretty good primer for a too-long-neglected New York City subculture.

Other notable documentaries I chanced upon were Janay Boulos and Abd Alkader Habak’s Birds of War , Jason Osder and William Lafi Youmans’s Who Killed Alex Odeh? , and Selina Miles’s Silenced . For decades, Sundance, in addition to its support of American independent film, has jump-started international documentaries like these three. May it continue to do so in the future.

"这一消息在电影开场中得到了呼应。在一个离家的父亲在旁白中谈论她们的场景之后不久——犹如来自坟墓彼端的呼声——三姐妹（大姐京、老二明日美和老小纪野）得知了父亲的死讯。和斋藤自己的父亲一样，女孩们的父亲自从父母离婚后就与家庭分居了。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“说实话，当我父亲去世时，我并没有感到难过，”斋藤说。“嗯，原因是我父母大约10年前离婚了，我已经有10年左右没见他了。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "电影在东京电影节的节目单中直言不讳地表达了其意图：探索失去亲人后随之而来的复杂情感，包括麻木。斋藤通过驱动《Kefi》大半部分的古怪幽默感来探讨这一点。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“我是个乐观的人；我父亲是个非常有趣的人。这也导致在他离世时并没有太多悲伤，我本以为自己很快会再见到他、跟他聊天，但这一切发生得太突然了，”斋藤说。“我意识到并不是每个人在失去挚爱时都会经历悲伤。所以这个想法油然而生，我想通过三姐妹来展现这种视角。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "片中的三姐妹在大部分片长里都是各自生活，而非展现她们之间重叠交织的动态。“仅仅因为你们是家人，你们并不总是在一起，也不是说你们总是、永远分享着某些东西，”斋藤说道。“你们的兄弟姐妹过着各自的生活，但在最后，兄弟姐妹或家人会思考同样的事情，或是拥有相同的心态。”电影中的其中一个章节最终让他们团聚。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这些差异体现在斋藤采用的混合视觉手法中，他游走于鲜艳色彩和单色黑白之间，也在混乱的手持摄影和更稳健的镜头运动之间切换。他并没有刻意按主题去分配这些视觉风格，不过他表示，这种结果让影像得以承载不同的细微差别。“这纯粹是因为我想测试和尝试不同的方法。这就是为什么它最终呈现出现在的样子，”他说道，并补充道：“我认为保持观众的兴趣和专注是很重要的。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "斋藤的试验源于他亲力亲为的工作方式——他身兼导演、编剧、摄影师、灯光师和剪辑师多职——而揽下这些角色主要归结于得心应手，这也是他习惯的拍电影方式。“这就是为什么我的风格是使用单反相机，我用iMovie剪辑，让我的朋友们作为演员出镜。我在YouTube上就是这么做的，在规模更大的制作中我也在幕后工作，”他说。“但是当你置身于更大制作的大片场时，有时并非所有人的方向都一致，因此当你试图拍电影时，有时那会变成一种干扰。所以我真正想做的是只和那些我真正信任的人一起拍电影。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《Kefi》的诞生或许也反映了一种渴望，即展现一系列打破国际社会对日本电影固有理解的创作方法。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "“当人们想到由日本人制作的日本电影时，大家会想到动漫或具有[主流吸引力]的电影，”斋藤说。“但我认为这很遗憾。我觉得世界上有更多有趣、滑稽、独特的日本面孔，所以我真的很想通过电影向全世界展示这一点。”", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "斋藤表示，他在电影中身兼多职或许能更直接地向观众传达他的观点。“我只是想证明，日本电影不仅有小津或黑泽明这样的大师，还有像滨口（龙介）这样的现代创作者，甚至是像我这样的人。这就是我的志向。”", "translated": true}]

article_text:
Likely the strangest entry at this year’s Tokyo International Film Festival , the surreal “ Kefi ,” the debut feature by cinematographer Saito Kisin, mixes multiple short stories and multiple styles to make sense of the feelings around a complicated relationship with his late father.

It doesn’t get there through the signifiers one might anticipate: there are aliens, dinosaurs, dream affairs and more across the film’s compact runtime. “Kefi” plays in the festival’s Nippon Cinema Now section.

“Initially, I wanted to do four series of short films and put it together, and that would become a feature,” Saito says. “And those four would all have individual themes. So the first one would be ethics. Second would be hypocrisy. There would be discrimination, and fourth would be life and death.”

The youngest of three brothers, Saito intended to loosely connect the project to his own family, with his shorts following three sisters instead. Then, in 2024, he received news that his father had died.

That news is echoed in the film’s opening. Shortly after a scene in which their absent father speaks about them in narration, an echo from beyond the grave, three sisters – oldest Kyo, middle child Asumi and youngest Kino – learn of his death. Like Saito’s own father, the girls’ father had been separated from the family since their parents’ divorce.

“To tell you the truth, when my father passed, I didn’t feel sad,” Saito says. “Well, the reason being my parents divorced about 10 years ago, I haven’t met him for about 10 or so years.”

The film’s listing in the Tokyo program is upfront about its aim to explore the complicated feelings that follow a loss, including numbness. Saito explores that through the oddball humor that drives much of “Kefi.”

“I’m an optimistic person; my father was a very funny guy. That also added to the fact that there wasn’t much grief in his loss, and I thought that I would meet again with him and talk with him again soon, but that became so sudden,” Saito says. “I realized that not everybody goes through grief when they lose their loved ones. So that idea came to me, and I wanted to depict that perspective through the three sisters.”

The three sisters spend much of the film’s runtime apart, rather than the film exploring an overlapping dynamic between them. “Just because you’re family, you’re not always together, it’s not like you always share something, always,” Saito says. “Your siblings lead their separate lives, but at the very end, siblings or families think about the same things or have the same mindset.” One episode of the film eventually reunites them.

Those differences are embodied in the mixed visual approaches Saito takes, switching between vivid color and monochrome, and between chaotic handheld work and steadier camerawork. He didn’t set out to assign those looks along thematic lines, though he says the result allowed the imagery to carry different nuances. “It’s only because I wanted to test and try different approaches. That’s why it ended up as it is,” he says, adding: “I think it’s important that people stay interested and will be attentive.”

Saito’s experiments come from his hands-on approach – he is credited as director, writer, cinematographer, gaffer and editor – and taking on those roles mostly comes down to comfort, as it’s the way he knows how to make films. “That’s why my style is to use a single-lens reflex camera, I use iMovie and have my friends appear as actors. That’s what I use for YouTube, and I work behind the camera on bigger productions as well,” he says. “But when you’re on a big set with bigger productions, sometimes not everybody’s looking in the same direction, and so sometimes that becomes kind of a noise when you’re trying to make a film. And so what I really wanted to do was make a film only with people I really trust.”

The making of “Kefi” also perhaps reflects a desire to show a range of approaches that stand out from the international understanding of Japanese film.

“When you think about Japanese films done by Japanese people, people would imagine anime or films with [mainstream appeal],” Saito says. “But I think that’s a shame. I feel that there’s more interesting, more funny, more unique Japanese people in the world, so I really want to show that to people around the world through film.”

Saito says his multiple roles on the film may convey his point of view more directly to the audience. “I just want to prove that Japanese films are not only about those classic filmmakers like Ozu or Kurosawa, but there are more modern people like Hamaguchi, or even myself. That is my aspiration.”

article_text:
Source: Universal / Paramount / Disney

‘Forgotten Island’, ‘Street Fighter’, ‘Whalefall’

Universal animation Forgotten Island leads new releases in UK and Ireland cinemas this weekend as Paramount’s Street Fighter and Disney’s Whalefall also launch.

Universal launches DreamWorks’ animation Forgotten Island in 634 venues. The film, which follows two best friends who become stranded in a mystical world, has been rolling out internationally over the last month and is up to $50m worldwide so far. It is DreamWorks’ first wholly originally title since 2023’s Ruby Gillman, Teenage Kraken which opened on £886,000 from 567 sites before reaching a £2.6m cume.

Directed by Joel Crawford and Januel Mercado, Forgotten Island features voices from musician H.E.R., Jenny Slate and Dave Franco.

Paramount opens Kitao Sakurai’s action title Street Fighter in 594 locations. It is the second film this year to be adapted from a martial arts-based video game, following Mortal Kombat 2 – that title debuted in May with £1.6m for Warner Bros and a £3.4m total. The video game was previously adapted in 1995 starring Jean-Claude Van Damme and went on to earn £2.3m at the box office for Sony.

Survival thriller Whalefall is launching in 500 cinemas for Disney. Austin Abrams stars in Brian Duffield’s film as a scuba diver who gets swallowed up by a sperm whale and has just one hour to get out before his oxygen tank runs out. The film may be able to ride the waves of Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil , which also stars Abrams having a particularly bad day and is approaching £13m at the UK box office.

NAZA doc gets release

In event titles, Trafalgar Releasing is screening Hadestown: The Musical in 542 sites after opening on Tuesday (October 13); music documentary Always Lalisa in 143 sites after opening October 12; and Macbeth - Met Opera 2026 in 45 sites on Saturday (October 17). Cinematik has ENB: The Sleeping Beauty .

In re-releases, Park Circus screens 2001 horror The Others in 217 venues while Anime Ltd 4K has screenings of 2010 anime Arrietty in 87 venues.

Lesley Manville stars in Winter Of The Crow which Signature Entertainment opens in 67 cinemas. Kasia Adamik’s thriller follows a British scholar who visits Cold War-era Poland as the country enters martial law in 1981. It premiered in Toronto’s Platform section.

Source: mk2 Films

‘NAZA’

The Venice award-winning documentary NAZA opens in 55 locations via Dogwoof, after previewing in 104 cinemas on Thursday (October 15). Directed by Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, the film details interviews with Israeli soldiers and intelligence officers who bear witness to the genocidal killing of Palestinians, including many civilians, in their homes and apartments in Gaza. It won the special jury prize in Venice. Abraham and Szor were two of four directors behind Oscar-winning doc No Other Land , about the occupied West Bank, which totalled £141,000 during its box office run in 2024.

In Indian cinema, Bakrania Media has courtroom drama Prahaar in 42 sites while AA Films is screening horror comedy Nayyi Navelli in 41.

French crime drama Case 137 is out in 27 venues via Conic Film. Dominik Moll directs this docudrama about an investigator who polices the police and is tasked with a difficult case. It premiered in Cannes competition in 2025 and went on to be nominated for eight Cesar awards, winning best actress for Lea Drucker.

Further releases include Taiwanese dystopian Deadline via DOVC UK; Irish political biopic Forever Is Now via Soilsiu Films; Chinese sports drama It’s My Time via Central City Media; Peruvian melodrama Mistura via Exposure; and horror title The Influencer Project via Icon Film Distribution.

article_text:
A judge overseeing Russell Brand’s criminal trial has dismissed an indecent assault charge against the British comedian and actor, replacing it with a count of attempted indecent assault.

Mr Justice Bennathan made the decision midway through the trial, telling jurors that he had concluded there was “insufficient evidence” to support the indecent assault charge in connection with an alleged incident involving a female MTV employee in 2001, according to Sky News.

'Fourth Wing' TV Series Casts Esther McGregor and Emilio Sakraya as Violet Sorrengail and Xaden Riorson

The allegation relates to an incident in which Brand allegedly grabbed the woman by the arm and tried to drag her into a toilet.

The judge subsequently added a charge of attempted indecent assault to the indictment, relating to the same alleged incident. While Brand has been formally acquitted of the original indecent assault count, jurors will still be asked to consider whether he attempted to commit the alleged offense. To formalize the decision, the judge selected one juror to deliver a not-guilty verdict on the original charge.

Describing the procedure as a “slightly artificial process,” Bennathan told the jury, “The defendant Russell Brand has entered a not-guilty plea to this count.”

The development came after the court heard four police statements given by Brand.

Brand, 51, who rose to fame as a stand-up comedian and television presenter before launching a Hollywood career with films including “Forgetting Sarah Marshall” and “Get Him to the Greek,” has denied all allegations of wrongdoing.

The trial at London’s Southwark Crown Court centers on allegations made by six women concerning incidents dating from 1999 to 2009. Brand originally faced seven charges, including three counts of rape, three of sexual assault and one of indecent assault.

The proceedings have featured testimony from several women who have accused Brand of sexual misconduct. Last week, a fourth accuser told the court that Brand had sexually assaulted her while she was working at a radio station in 2004 or 2005. She alleged that he pushed her against a wall, forcibly kissed her and touched her breasts and buttocks while people accompanying him looked on without intervening.

During the prosecution’s opening arguments, Riel Karmy-Jones KC described Brand as “ruthless and calculated,” alleging that his sexual appetite was “indiscriminate and voracious.” Prosecutors have argued that the six women, who did not know one another, came forward independently.

The criminal investigation followed a joint investigation by The Sunday Times and Channel 4’s “Dispatches” in September 2023, which brought allegations of rape, sexual assault and emotional abuse against Brand into the public eye.

Brand has pleaded not guilty to all seven charges against him.

article_text:
Week in wildlife: a friendly seal, a furious goldcrest and ‘the swanfather’

This week’s best wildlife photographs from around the world

Fri 9 Oct 2026 03.00 EDT

Comedy Wildlife Photography awards 2026 . Wittmer said: “During my photo trip to the island of Helgoland, Germany, I encountered a goldcrest for the first time – and it was love at first sight. Europe’s smallest bird wandered right in front of me, presumably searching for food. To get a perspective at eye level, I placed my camera on the ground. My heart was pounding and my finger was glued to the shutter as the tiny bird darted back and forth. Suddenly, it came to a stop and looked straight at the camera”Photograph: Jan Wittmer/Comedy Wildlife awards 2026

Living Planet report , the World Wildlife Fund writes: “In 2010, only around 3,200 wild tigers remained, and the species seemed to be sliding toward extinction. By 2025, the population had grown to roughly 5,700, an increase of more than 70%”Photograph: Andy Rouse/WWF/PA

wētāpunga , the world’s heaviest insect, in New Zealand. The flightless cricket, which can be up to 10cm (4in) long, used to be found across the North Island, but by the 1990s had retreated to a few smaller islands. However, a new breeding programme has released 11,000 wētāpunga into the wild – grounds for hope for the species’ futurePhotograph: Anton Sorokin/Alamy

parrots were seized by customs staff at the port of Pozzallo, Sicily, Italy. They were found in a car about to board a catamaran bound for Malta. The driver of the car, rather ambitiously, had hoped to smuggle out 300 tortoises and 77 parrots, many of which were protected species. {"type": "paragraph", "text": "ビールを口にしながら、ゼノはこうした作品を深夜に制作していたことを明かした。現在もその習慣は変わらず、夜11時に制作を始め、朝7時に就寝するという。「私の邪魔をするような人は、みんな眠っていますから。料理をする必要もなければ、家を掃除する必要もありません」"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": 「ここにあるのはちょっと変わった作品です」

コゼット・ゼノは自身が手がけた《Let’s Go Higher》（1952）を指差しながらそう語った。プエルトリコ大学在学中に制作したこの作品には、霞がかった風景のなかに無数の立方体が描かれ、その表面を小さな人物たちがよじ登っている。立方体には窓がなく、何に使われるものなのかもわからない。

「常に上を目指せ」

ゼノに会ったのは、リチャード・ソルトーンのニューヨーク拠点だ。同ギャラリーでは10月30日まで、1950年代の作品を集めた小規模な回顧展が開催されている。そこでゼノが注目を促したのは、《Let’s Go Higher》に描かれた立方体のうち、唯一出入り口が設けられたものだった。その緑色の構造物は、内部から光を放つコンテナのように見える。立方体の上には1人の人物が立ち、誇らしげに周囲を指し示している。「彼は『常に上を目指せ。決して下がるな』と言っているんです」と、ゼノは笑顔で語った。

この言葉は、1950年代に創作活動を始め、近年になってようやく世界的な評価を得たゼノの歩みとも重なる。

96歳のゼノは、近年開催された2つの大規模な シュルレアリスム 展でも強い存在感を示した。ひとつは、2021年から2022年にかけて メトロポリタン美術館 （MET）と テート・モダン で開催された、シュルレアリスムの世界的な広がりを紹介する展覧会。もうひとつは、2024年にテキサス州のフォートワース近代美術館で開催された、カリブ海地域における シュルレアリスムの展開を探る展覧会 だ。

1950年代、ゼノはシュルレアリスムの創始者の1人である アンドレ・ブルトン と交流を深めた。ヨーロッパではシュルレアリスムの作家たちとともに展覧会に参加したものの、長らく美術史のなかで正当な評価を得ることはなかった。その背景には、ゼノが女性だったことに加え、欧米中心の美術史研究がカリブ海地域の作家に十分目を向けてこなかったこともあるのかもしれない。

また、美術史家のホイットニー・チャドウィックが指摘するように、女性のシュルレアリスム作家の多くは、自らをこの運動の一員とは考えていなかった。その理由のひとつに、男性作家たちから疎外されていると感じていたことが挙げられる。 メレット・オッペンハイム 、 レオノーラ・キャリントン 、レメディオス・バロといった画家たちも、美術史のなかで長らく周縁的な存在として 扱われてきた が、現在ではシュルレアリスムの歴史を語るうえで欠かせない作家とみなされている。そこで、ゼノ自身にシュルレアリスム作家を自認しているか尋ねると、彼女はこう答えた。

「私は自分のことをシュルレアリスム作家だと思っています。かれらと同じ自由の精神を持っていますから。自分に制限を設けることはありません。今も新しいことに挑戦し続けていますよ」

夢と現実のあいだで生まれる作品

ゼノのシュルレアリスム的な発想は、前述の展覧会にも出品された《Ni hablar del peluquín（小さなかつらについて語っても仕方がない）》（1952）に色濃く表れている。この作品には、肉体がグロテスクに絡み合ったような塊が描かれ、ところどころから毛がのぞいている。それが作品名にあるかつらの毛なのか、それとも陰毛なのかは判然としない。

「これは男性を表しているんです」とゼノは語った。そして、作品の性的なニュアンスにも触れ、こう続けた。「彼はいろいろなことを考えています。何を考えているのかは、見る人が自由に想像していいんです。かつらをかぶっているので、若い男性ではありませんね」

サルバドール・ダリ や マックス・エルンスト 、 ルネ・マグリット といった男性のシュルレアリスム作家たちは、欲望や好奇心の対象として女性の裸体を描くことで知られていた。対照的にゼノは、これまでに裸の女性を描いたのは1度だけだと振り返る。その理由を尋ねると、彼女は「男性が好きですから」と冗談めかして答えた。

ビールを口にしながら、ゼノはこうした作品を深夜に制作していたことを明かした。現在もその習慣は変わらず、夜11時に制作を始め、朝7時に就寝するという。「私の邪魔をするような人は、みんな眠っていますから。料理をする必要もなければ、家を掃除する必要もありません」

多くのシュルレアリスム作家は、自らの作品を夢になぞらえてきた。ほかの人々が眠っている時間帯に制作するゼノの習慣も、こうした夢との関わりを連想させる。キューバのシュルレアリスム作家、ウィフレド・ラムがかつて語った「眠っていないとき、私は夢を見る」という言葉も思い起こされる。しかし、深夜の制作についてゼノは、「自分が何をしているのか、はっきりと意識している」と語った。

プエルトリコで芽生えた創作の原点

ゼノは1930年、ドミニカ共和国に生まれた。当時の同国は政情不安が続いた末、独裁者ラファエル・トルヒーヨが権力を握ったばかりだった。ゼノはまだ幼い頃、家族とともにプエルトリコへ亡命した。「サントドミンゴのことはまったく知らないんです。だから私は自分をプエルトリコ人だと言っています」と彼女は言う。

プエルトリコのオールド・サンフアンで育ったゼノは、周囲に広がる山々や海に親しむようになった。「プエルトリコでは、どこにいても海が見えます。水中の泡に紛れた小さな魚を見るために、祖母はよく朝6時に海へ連れて行ってくれました。いつもシュノーケリングをしていましたね」。そして、ゼノは「私にとって、自然はとても身近な存在なんです」と付け加えた。

幼い頃から親しんできた自然は、ゼノの初期作品にも表れている。油性クレヨンで描かれた《Reunion 1》と《Reunion 2》（ともに1952）には、渦を巻くような白い形が入り交じり、水の流れに翻弄される貝殻を思わせる。これらは、ゼノが父親の仕事を通じて手に入れたクラフト紙に描かれたものだ。また、《Tropical Haze》（1954）では、緑がかった背景につるのような線が走り、身近な植物から着想を得たことがうかがえる。

ゼノが大学に入学した頃、プエルトリコは大きな変革期を迎えていた。1950年にはアメリカの統治に反発する武装蜂起が各地で起こり、独立を求める機運が高まった。芸術家たちも、民族自決を求める動きを後押しする役割を担うようになった。

ゼノが師事したのは、スペイン出身のシュルレアリスム作家エウヘニオ・グラネルだ。グラネルはスペイン内戦で共和派に加わり、敗戦後に亡命を余儀なくされ、カリブ海地域へと渡った人物だ。独立を求める機運が高まるなか、ゼノはその思いをシュルレアリスムの表現に織り込んだ。その一例としてゼノが挙げたのが、1951年の絵画《Safe Journey》だ。この作品には、ダイヤモンドでできたアーチの下を船が進む様子が描かれている。ゼノによれば、このアーチは「プエルトリコは貧しい国だが、決して貧しいわけではない」ということを表している。また、船に襲いかかろうとする恐ろしげな怪物も描かれているが、この怪物は目が見えない。ゼノは「脅威にはなりません。何の力ももっていないんです」と説明した。

1953年にプエルトリコ大学を卒業したゼノは、大学院の奨学金を得てパリのエコール・デュ・ルーブルに留学した。そこでシュルレアリスムの創始者の1人であるブルトンと出会った。ゼノはブルトンに強く傾倒し、のちに自身の娘に彼が1928年に発表した著書『ナジャ』にちなんだ名前を付けた。

96歳になっても衰えない創作意欲

当時、ゼノの両親はキューバで暮らしており、1954年には父親の病気をきっかけに、彼女もカリブ海地域へ戻ることになった。しかし、その後も政情不安に翻弄され、キューバから二度、出国を余儀なくされたという。最初のきっかけは、路上で大量に血を流している男性を目撃したことだった。繊維会社で働いていたゼノは急いで職場に戻り、フルヘンシオ・バティスタ（*1）政権による弾圧の危険性を同僚に訴えた。ところが、その同僚は実は諜報員で、すぐにキューバを離れるよう彼女に促したという。その後、アメリカで結婚したゼノは、カストロ政権下のキューバに暮らす両親を訪ねた。だが1961年、カストロによる通貨改革で手持ちの金が価値を失い、再びキューバを離れざるを得なくなった。

*1 キューバ革命以前に同国を支配していた独裁者。

ゼノはこれまで何度も住まいを移してきたが、現在は孫娘が暮らすミズーリ州ジャクソンを拠点に活動している。本人によれば、これまで専用のアトリエを構えたことはなく、制作を完全に中断した時期もあったという。そのひとつが、夫のロバート・ベイツを亡くした年だった。

それでもゼノは現在も制作を続けており、実物大のドア4枚にまたがる新作について生き生きと語った。制作のきっかけは、アトランタにホテルを開業する予定の孫息子から、壁画を依頼されたことだった。しかし、ゼノはそこから構想を変え、ドアを使った作品に取り組むことにした。現在はドアを床に置き、本人が「海の要素」と表現するモチーフを描いている。この作品は12月、アートフェア「Untitled Art, Miami Beach」に出展するリチャード・ソルトーンのブースで披露される予定だ。

ドアを使ったこの作品は、独特な色彩の立方体が描かれた《Let’s Go Higher》の出入り口を思い起こさせる。ゼノはインタビューのなかで、同作に込めた意味を改めてこう語った。「決して下がらず、常に上を目指すんです」

2024年は シュルレアリスム 誕生100周年にあたる。これを祝うとともに、これまでこの運動について語るときに見過ごされてきたヨーロッパ以外の地域や女性アーティストにも光を当て、ベスト作品32点を紹介する。

article_text:
Source: BFI/I/Neil Massey

Ben Roberts and Gaëtan Bruel

Gaëtan Bruel, president of the CNC, has rallied for stronger UK-French collaboration, telling an audience of UK and French producers at a BFI London Film Festival event: “We need you to be more ambitious about what France and the UK can create together.”

He spoke at a reception as part of the fourth iteration of the New Waves programme, which runs during the BFI London Film Festival, at London’s Institut Français.

The New Waves programme aims to foster collaboration between UK and French producers, with a programme of meetings and events held from October 8-10. Sixteen UK producers took part, including Debbie Gray of Genesius Pictures, Erebus Pictures’ Helen Simmons, Shudder Films’ Jack Tarling, Bêtes Sauvages’ James Watson and See-Saw Films’ Lily Brook.

From France, 12 producers included Jean-Benoît Gillig of Léonis Productions, Justin Pechberty of Les Valseurs and 24 25 Films’ Thibault Gast.

Bruel called on UK filmmakers and producers to “bring us more projects, come and work with French producers,” and pointed towards LFF opening night film Elsinore as an example of UK and French collaboration thanks to the involvement of French-owned Studiocanal and Pathe.

Concrete projects

He pointed to the CNC’s Aide aux Cinémas du Monde (World Cinema Aid) fund, which last year increased its budget to €8m, and is open to non-French filmmakers wishing to co-produce with France. “There is sometimes a misconception about this fund – it’s not reserved for filmmakers from a particular part of the world; British filmmakers can apply, international filmmakers based in Britain can apply,” he said.

UK-France co-productions to access this fund have included Sandhya Suri’s Cannes 2024 premiere Santosh , Jessica Hausner’s Cannes 2023 premiere Club Zero and Rungano Nyoni’s 2017 Directors’ Fortnight title I Am Not A Witch.

BFI CEO Ben Roberts flagged the UK Global Screen Fund as the UK’s “invitation to partner and co-produce. We have tools at our disposal.”

From the French perspective, the UK’s links to the US industry are valuable. “You are deeply part of the European creative community, while also being closely connected to the American industry, and few countries are better placed to help keep both sides around the same table,” said Bruel.

Of the relationship between the two countries post-Brexit, Bruel noted, “The CNC and the BFI made a very deliberate choice. Our institutional relationship should not become weaker simply because the political framework around us had changed. Over the past few years, we have tried to make this relationship increasingly relevant… Our producers meet regularly, our teams exchange constantly.”

“The resilience of our friendship with our friends at the CNC has been one of our guiding north stars,” said Roberts. “What I would call the mycelium network of creativity and financial networks and distribution relationships that exist between the UK and France are very deeply connected.”

Last year, the CNC signed a Moving Image Cooperation Agreement with the BFI – the first time the BFI has done so with a European country – and a memorandum of understanding with the British Film Commission (BFC).

“Let’s say that institutions can build bridges, but ultimately producers and filmmakers have to cross them,” said Bruel. “Here we have some room for improvement, but looking at the quality of the producers gathered here on both sides of the channel, I am convinced that the potential is here. The question is how we can now turn that potential into more concrete projects.”

article_text:
Films and events

Family

Relaxed screening: A Mighty Adventure

Relaxed screenings

House lights will remain on a low level throughout the screening, and the volume will be turned down. Audience members will be able to make noise, stim freely, move around or leave and return during the screening.

We will provide a sanctuary space for you to use near the auditorium.

See other screenings of this film

This lovingly crafted, dialogue-free animated tale follows a trio of insects who undertake an epic journey.

Credits

Director-screenwriter Toe Yuen

Taiwan-Malaysia-Hong Kong (S.A.R of China) 2026. 77min

Courtesy of Golden Network Asia

Language Dialogue free

Access information

Wednesday 14 October 18:20

Relaxed screening

Find out about booking access tickets

Introduction

A butterfly and a grasshopper are removed from the forest and taken to an apartment in the city. Here, they befriend a spider who tries to help them on the long journey back home, which is fraught with dangerous challenges. This innovative and engrossing animated adventure transports us into a familiar world, albeit from the microcosmic perspective of its protagonists.

Justin Johnson

Before the screening

Doors will open 30 minutes before the screening start time.

No trailers will be shown.

The programme will be introduced.

During the screening

Our house lights will remain on a low level throughout the screening, and the volume will be turned slightly down.

You will be able to leave the auditorium and return during the screening.

You will be able to make noise.

We will provide a quiet space for you to use near the auditorium.

You are welcome to take refreshments into the cinema but no hot food please. For information on BFI Bar & Kitchen and BFI Riverfront please see our food and drink page .

How to book

Find out about booking access tickets .

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

article_text:
On his campaign website, Xavier Becerra has a page devoted to Hollywood. The 1,600-word policy statement is long on platitudes — “California Is the Home of Film and TV and We Intend to Keep It That Way” — but short on concrete promises.

It may also have been written with artificial intelligence. According to Pangram, a widely used AI detector, “100% of this text is AI,” though the campaign denies it.

Related Stories

'Women and War,' About Ukrainian Women Undergoing Trauma Therapy, Acquired by Rise and Shine World Sales (EXCLUSIVE)

‘Hazara Town,’ About the Hazara Community in Pakistan, Acquired by Filmotor Ahead of IDFA World Premiere (EXCLUSIVE)

“These AI assessors are notoriously inaccurate,” said Jonathan Underland, Becerra’s spokesman.

Becerra is cruising toward the California gubernatorial election with a 20-point lead in the polls and a 96% chance of victory in the prediction markets. He has denied most requests for interviews and has avoided making firm commitments on a range of issues from AI to housing to electric vehicles.

On the campaign trail, he has turned his lack of promises into part of his pitch.

“It’s easy when you’re a candidate to make all sorts of promises. It’s harder to prove you can deliver,” he said at a stop in Glendale on Monday. “Vote for someone who knows how to deliver, because the promises go away after Election Day.”

Introducing Becerra to the crowd, Assemblyman John Harabedian offered a similar line: “He is someone who will underpromise and overdeliver.”

Assuming he is elected, Becerra will face immediate calls to expand the state’s incentive for film and TV production, now capped at $750 million a year. Even if Congress passes a federal film incentive, state lawmakers argue that California must do more to compete for film jobs. Attorney General Rob Bonta has said he will sponsor a bill to eliminate the cap entirely.

“We do need to, early next year, take steps to strengthen it,” said Rick Chavez Zbur, the Burbank Assemblyman who is one of Hollywood’s best allies in Sacramento. “A number of us have wanted to uncap the program for some time.”

Another proposal is to include “above the line” salaries — actors, directors, etc. — in the program. Such ideas would cost money — maybe a lot of money — and would have to be reconciled with the state’s other fiscal priorities.

How would Becerra do that? At the event on Monday, the candidate was not much more definitive than his website.

“I will support anything that will help us keep Hollywood in Hollywood,” he said. “We have to fight for this industry.”

Asked whether he supports eliminating the $750 million cap or including “above the line” costs, he was noncommittal.

“I’ll sit down with all the legislators to see what kind of proposals are put before us,” he said. “But we’re going to fight.”

Becerra’s Republican opponent, Steve Hilton , has vowed to eliminate the cap and to include above-the-line costs. According to Pangram, Hilton’s film policy was also written by AI, though because it is shorter and mostly made up of bulleted lists, rather than complete sentences, it is harder for Pangram to analyze. (The Hilton campaign declined to comment.)

Becerra’s film platform includes some of the tells of AI writing, such as the “it’s not this, it’s that” construction: “California did not just produce the film industry. It built it.”

Ironically, it also endorses a state mandate for AI disclosure by productions.

Underland said that AI was not used to brainstorm or develop the platform in any way.

“We don’t do that,” he said. “We don’t talk to AI about policy. We talk to people about policy.”

Pangram claims a false positive rate of 1 in 10,000, and claims the tool is especially accurate when reviewing political speeches, with human writing flagged as AI 0.0% of the time. Independent research has also backed up Pangram’s accuracy.

Last month, the Economist used Pangram to analyze parliamentary speeches, finding that 10% of the words spoken in the British Parliament were drafted with AI. AI use was also prevalent in Australia, Canada and the U.S. When the speakers were asked about it, the most common response was “surprise and denial,” the publication reported.

The Hilton campaign has used AI to create campaign ads , and has disclosed that usage in accordance with state law . In one such ad, an AI-generated Becerra endorses the idea of sending out a “vague policy tweet” — “Great idea, but keep it vague like all the other ones. Not too much detail.”

Becerra’s campaign has said it does not use AI in its videos, and has criticized Hilton’s “AI slop.” The state AI disclosure requirement covers audio, video and images, but does not extend to text.

At the campaign event, Becerra denied that his policy statement was AI-generated.

“No,” he said, “that’s absolutely incorrect.”

article_text:
Hollywood’s feted genius, chessmaster, international man of mystery; yet a simple Jewish mama’s boy, insatiably curious, who retained his plainspoken Bronx drawl and unconditional adoration of his family and pets to his dying day; across thirteen feature films in just under half a century, the greatest enduring gift of Stanley Kubrick may be his obliteration of boundaries. A formalist of myriad forms, a deeply intellectual filmmaker whose most powerful images came surging from the unconscious, a mighty humanist and acerbic misanthrope, a consummate artist and blockbuster showman whose work is equally adored by artists and scientists, film scholars, midnight-movie fiends, and the general public. To this day, no label can contain Kubrick. To appreciate him is to stand in awe of the revelation that radical formal experimentation, intellectual curiosity, and mass-cultural appeal—contrary to widely held belief—do not need to be enemies. Genre does not need to be a lower form; story structure does not need to stifle spontaneity and mystery. Here is a man who did it all and left behind the sense that he’d barely got started.

Criterion’s new 4K Stanley Kubrick collection presents, for the very first time, a comprehensive box featuring every single one of the master’s completed films, from his early shorts to trailblazing features with MGM and Warner Bros., stunningly restored and with a rich selection of desserts and hors d’oeuvres. Across thirteen discs, we’ve had the incalculable pleasure of revisiting his full body of work, including commentaries and supplements as old as the heyday of LaserDisc and as new as this year (prepare to learn how HAL-9000 predicted LLM “hallucinations” as you buckle in for Luca Guadagnino’s 2001 -conversant Artificial ), as well as a set of enlightening documentaries about the director and his work, some of them newly restored.

In celebration of this milestone in Kubrick collecting, and in hopes of a Kubrick renaissance with a moviegoing public starved for true boldness and invention in the film industry, we’ve decided to roll out a season of features dedicated to the filmmaker’s oeuvre and beyond, going through Criterion’s box era by era and disc by disc—plus a couple of surprises from the archives. For those who haven’t yet earned their bachelor’s in Kubrickology, we hope we can sway you to fill in your gaps. And for those who know Stanley ball, we hope we can make you misty-eyed on a nostalgic trip to the outer limits. Welcome to our season of Kubrick.

Features

Part I: Early Documentary Shorts, Fear and Desire , and Killer’s Kiss

Part II: The Killing , Paths of Glory , and Spartacus

Coming soon.

Part III: Lolita , Dr. Strangelove , and 2001: A Space Odyssey

Coming soon.

Part IV: A Clockwork Orange , Barry Lyndon , and The Shining

Coming soon.

Part V: Full Metal Jacket and Eyes Wide Shut

Coming soon.

Interviews

“He Wanted the Films to Survive”: Michael Chaiken on Assembling Criterion’s The Complete Kubrick

“That Cut Is Stanley’s Cut”: Nigel Galt on Editing Eyes Wide Shut with Kubrick

Plus, stay tuned for more from the Kubrick archive!

The Complete Kubrick is now available through the Criterion Collection .

article_text:
Dustin Hoffman , who shot to fame after starring as Ben Braddock in Mike Nichols’ classic film “ The Graduate ,” has opened up about his experience shooting the 1967 comedy-drama in a recent essay for The New Yorker , which he described as having been a “terrible experience” despite the fact that the movie changed his life.

“I felt immediately uncomfortable, unworthy. Here I was, playing a starring role in a movie by Mike Nichols, who was the director of the moment, but I felt like I had no right to be there,” writes Hoffman early in the piece of his time on set. “It was a terrible experience making the movie that changed my life.” Much of his anxiety stemmed from worrying that Nichols “was angry at me, either because I was doing something wrong or because he had realized what everybody else already knew, that he had miscast the lead in his film.”

Hoffman writes that the film “exacerbated all my insecurities from the start.” “When my agent said that Mike was interested in me, I didn’t even want to try out for the part. I had read the Charles Webb novel that Mike was adapting, and it was obvious that I was all wrong for Benjamin. A track star and straight-A student, the head of the debate team—this was an affluent, all-American kid, whose surname was ‘Braddock.’ Why would you cast a person who looks as ethnic as I do to play the ultimate Wasp? It made absolutely no sense.” He continued, explaining that his agent convinced him to screen-test for the role, which he ultimately got.

However, beyond Hoffman’s worries about his ability to play Ben, he also writes that Nichols was “frequently sour” on set, a “shocking, destabilizing” change from his personality during rehearsals. “I often felt that I was about to be fired. When we were shooting some of the film’s most famous sequences, I remember thinking, I have no fucking idea what I’m doing,” said Hoffman.

He also notes that while the director was “irritable with everyone,” there was a “certain sadism” that “seemed to creep in” only with him.

He continued: “There was a scene in which Katharine Ross had to slap me, and he made us do twenty-seven takes. The scene has Benjamin run into Elaine’s room, soaking wet from the rain, to tell her that he’s had an affair with an older woman; within seconds, Elaine realizes the woman is her mother. Mike just kept telling Katharine to hit me, to hit me harder. Katharine worried she would hurt me, and I told her, ‘I’m O.K. Just don’t hit my ear.’ Unfortunately, she missed a few times. I was dizzy by the end of that day, and Mike didn’t even use the slap in the film.”

The following day, Hoffman shot an underwater scene that required him to stay submerged in a scuba suit. “When I came up for air after a few takes, there was blood trickling out of my ear. Between all the slapping during the previous day and all the water pressure at the bottom of the pool, I’d punctured an eardrum,” he writes.

“The Graduate” first hit theaters on Dec. 22, 1967. Per its official description, the film followed a disillusioned college graduate (Hoffman) who finds himself torn between his older lover (Anne Bancroft) and her daughter (Ross). It was nominated for seven Oscars and was named the best picture winner at the 40th Academy Awards.

article_text:
広島県呉市に生まれ育った平井亨季（1996年生まれ）は、近年広島市と呉市という隣接したふたつの街の歴史と現在に着目し、ロトスコープによるアニメーション映像と立体模型、冊子によるテキストなどを組み合わせながら作品を制作しています。 平井は次のように語っています。「街の歴史と個人の記憶は相似形と言いたくなるほど似て感じられる時があります。私はこれまで作品の中で記憶すること、忘却することについて考えてきましたが、最近ではそれが広島に生まれ育ったことと無関係でないように思えてきました。それは昔から実はそうだったというよりも、広島／呉の歴史を知ることで似ているように見えてきたというのが実際だと思います。広島にまつわる様々な問いを知り、自分なりに思い浮かべる中で『私は広島／呉をどのように覚えていたいのか』という問いがいつも浮かんできます」と。 本展では、街の歴史と個人の記憶を重ねあわせて語る／描くことはセルフケアの実践となりえるのではないか、という平井の関心を起点に制作された新作を紹介します。「平和都市」と「軍港都市」の間、街の歴史と個人の記憶の間、記憶と忘却の間、映像と立体と冊子の間を行ったり来たりしながら、時間と空間がもつれるような感覚を味わってください。やがて「広島（呉）を少しでも多孔的で通気性のよい街として想像しようとしています」と語る平井の言葉に共感してもらえるでしょう。
